name: Vienna City Marathon
summary: The Vienna City Marathon starts at the Vienna International Centre and finishes on the Ringstrasse between the Burgtheater and City Hall. It passes the Prater, the State Opera and Schönbrunn Palace. Race guides describe it as a flat, fast road course.
courseHighlights: Start at the Vienna International Centre (UNO-City) and over the Reichsbrücke
Vienna State Opera and the Ringstrasse
Finish on the Ringstrasse between the Burgtheater and City Hall

paceStrategy.summary: The course is flat, so even pacing should work well. Use the early kilometres to settle in, then hold a steady rhythm through the city. Keep a little energy for the last kilometres on the Ringstrasse.

segments.terrain: Flat roads from the start over the Reichsbrücke
segments.advice: Run slightly under goal effort while the field is dense.
Lock into goal pace and stay relaxed.
Keep pace steady; even pacing pays off on a flat course.

segments.terrain: Flat city roads, finish on the Ringstrasse
segments.advice: Hold form and push in the last 2 km towards the finish.

fuelingNotes: The sources I used do not list aid-station positions, so check the official runner information. On a flat course, take gels at regular intervals, for example every 30–40 minutes.
tips: Race day can be cool in spring, so bring a throwaway layer for the start
The start is at UNO-City, away from the finish, so plan your transport
Crowds are dense early; line up in your correct start block

faq.question: Is the Vienna City Marathon flat?
faq.answer: Yes. Marathon Index lists a flat profile with about 75 m of total climbing, and a race listing gives a 44 m difference between the highest and lowest points.

faq.question: Where does the Vienna City Marathon finish?
faq.answer: The finish is on the Ringstrasse between the Burgtheater and City Hall, according to the Vienna tourist board.

faq.question: When is the Vienna City Marathon held?
faq.answer: It is usually held in April.
